n: Perhaps the best-loved psalm. David, once a shepherd himself, calls the Lord his shepherd. With God caring for him, he lacks nothing he truly needs. Jesus later called himself the Good Shepherd.
The shepherd lets his sheep rest in green pastures and leads them to quiet waters — rare and precious in the dry land of Israel. Sheep won’t drink from rushing streams.

f.g: Grassy meadows — precious in a dry land.
Literally “waters of rest” — calm, refreshing water.

n: He renews my life and guides me along right paths, because his own name and reputation are at stake in caring for me.

f.g: Brings me back, revives me — can also mean brings back a wandering sheep.
Right paths — trails that lead safely home.

n: Even walking through the darkest valley, David fears no harm, because the Shepherd is with him. His rod defends and his staff guides. Notice the shift from “he” to “you” — David now speaks to God directly.

f.w: the valley of the shadow of death
f.g: A valley of deep darkness — any frightening, dangerous place, including death itself.
The rod was a club for defense; the staff, a long crook for guiding and rescuing sheep.

n: The image shifts to a generous host: God sets a feast before David while his enemies watch, anoints his head with oil like an honored guest, and fills his cup to overflowing.

f.w: Thou preparest a table before me
thou anointest my head with oil
f.g: Anointing a guest’s head with oil was a sign of welcome and honor.

n: God’s goodness and steadfast love will pursue David all his life, and he will live in the Lord’s house forever. Latter-day Saints may think of the temple and of returning to dwell with God.

f.w: goodness and mercy shall follow me
f.g: “Follow” is literally “pursue” — God’s love chases after us. “Mercy” is ḥesed, covenant love.

f.w: dwell in the house of the LORD for ever
